newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax measures unlikely in 97 - Schaeuble.
newsitem.headline: German tax measures unlikely in 97 - Schaeuble.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's top deputy said on Friday he thought it unlikely that tax measures would be taken this year to help fill widening budget gaps.

"I don't believe the opportunity exists to solve the problem through fiscal measures in 1997," Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary group leader for the Christian Democrats (CDU), said on German television.
"We are in the middle of the year. We've said that we must discuss the 1998 budget thoroughly on the basis of the new figures," he added.

Schaeuble was speaking after Thursday's report of an estimated 18 billion mark shortfall in German 1997 tax revenues, raising further questions over the country's ability to qualify on time for the single European currency.
On a plan by finance minister Theo Waigel to use an upward reevaluation of Bundesbank gold reserves for budgetary purposes, Schaeuble stressed that this had no direct impact on current budget plans.
He said that any surplus gained from the measure would instead be set against historic debts arising from the unification of west Germany with the formerly Communist-controlled east in 1990.
